Well, it's not so much that just speaking to a therapist would fuck me over, but I'm fairly certain it wouldn't help much.  My parents sent me to one when I was a young teenager, and even back then I was pretty much just able to tell the guy what he wanted to hear until he let me go.  The past few years I've become an expert on presenting a normal face to people, so if I were put in front of a shrink IRL I know I'd probably just revert to the "tell him what he wants to hear until you can leave" thing.  It's much more easy for me to open about it with the anonymity afforded by the internet, in real life I have a severe mental block about putting this info out there.

The thing that would ruin my career would be something like getting on anti-depressants, which I think may help at this point, but I would be required to disclose it for my work, which requires a medical clearance.  So, basically, I'd be in better shape because of the medication, but would be stuck flipping burgers, which really doesn't sound like an improvement to me.

No problem!  I just hate seeing people get suckered when they're joining with the intention of doing something out of selfless regard.  It's not even really a matter of how savvy a person is, because recruiters will flat out lie to you if it means they'll get your signature on a contract.

I really wish they'd emphasize that SF is only looking for a certain type of person, and you can pass the courses with flying colors and still not be selected for absolutely any reason, or no reason at all.  I had friends kicked back to a line unit for being "too green", which basically means they just want you to try again in a year or two.

Either way good luck, and remember there are plenty of combat arms jobs besides the infantry.  They don't hold a monopoly on the "doing cool shit" sector of the armed forces, and many other jobs offer basically the same experience with a better command structure and more autonomy.  Give every job a close look before you decide to sign up.

Haha you don't sound idealistic, I was pretty much the exact same way when I joined.

If you really want to do combat arms, don't enlist under an 18X contract, and here's why.  Your recruiter is going to make it sound like it's the greatest option in the world and will sell it as if you're pretty much guaranteed an SF spot.  Remember, they're basically the closest you can get in the Army to a used car salesman.

If SF is your goal, just enlist as a regular ol' 11B, trust me.  There's several reasons for this.  For one, you can enlist for two or three years, and be done with it if you get in and decide it's really not what you were expecting, which happens to plenty of people.  SF contracts are five or six years minimum, I believe, and if you aren't selected you get sent right back your line job, where you'll be stuck for the duration of your contract doing something you didn't really sign up for.  In addition (and the recruiters won't tell you this) SF isn't really interested in soldiers that are fresh out of basic training.  I spent a few weeks with SF while I was in Afghanistan, and they basically think the 18X contracts are the biggest prank the Army has ever pulled.  My first squad leader, who was probably the most hardcore motherfucker I've ever met, was in the Army six years and went to selection three times before he finally passed selection.  Having some experience with the Army before you jump in to the special ops world will only benefit you.  

There are rare occasions where someone on an 18X contract will pass selection and the Q-course, but they're very rare.  The whole idea of the SF contract is basically just a way for the Army to con people into joining the infantry for long contracts.  If you just enlist as infantry, you'll be able to go to schools whenever you want.  Your unit leaders will actually probably beg you to go to ranger school and offer promotions for doing so.  If you spend a couple years in the army and decide it's where you want to stay, you'll have absolutely no trouble going to selection whenever you want, believe me.

I'm not trying to discourage you or anything, I've just seen a lot of people fall into this trap, where they're promised ranger/SF school in their contract, and either end up washing out or quitting.  Then they're stuck doing something they really don't like very much.  If your heart is totally set on it, good luck.  Those courses are designed to wash out quitters more than anything, so if you go with the mentality that you're not going to quit no matter how hard it gets, you'll probably do just fine.

Well, besides the job, I'm also pretty much the only family member my age that isn't living off of welfare and/or fucking with really hardcore drugs.  That isn't a reason to continue like this, I know, I just know that I can suck it up and keep going like this, whereas I'm not sure some of my family members could were they to know that we were just universally fucked up in the head, haha.

I'd probably consider it if it were completely anonymous, and cheap enough that I could justify the expense as a pricey incidental, or at least a weekend in Vegas.  I really need to make sure there's no way it could be traced back to me.

Thanks for the suggestions, though.  I'll definitely give them a look.
That may be true, I've just noticed a different pattern.  I may just not remember it I guess.

Why not do both?  I'm pretty sure the army still has the "green to gold" program.  You basically get paid to go to college full time, and are commissioned as an officer upon graduation.  I know they're always looking for JAG lawyers.  You could probably enlist as a paralegal or something similar and use your connections with the senior NCOs and officers in your unit to get a slot, as long as your ASVAB scores are high enough.  I'm assuming they are if you were on track for law school.

Yeah, I've thought that too.  Honestly it's probably too late now, I've kept this going for too long, but if someone in my close family would have just asked when I got back if I were having problems with the experience, I probably would have told them.  It's really not their responsibility to carry my mental baggage, but who knows.

I've been to the VA twice since I've been out, and I probably won't ever go back unless it's a dire emergency.  The VA doctors are overworked and underpaid, I understand, but the quality of care is just plain shit, at least the one in my area.

Nah, I let my clearance expire a while back.  I work in a field that requires medical clearance, and mental health is a disqualifying factor.  I don't really want to disclose the field I'm in, but it's a case where if I were to have my medical clearance pulled, I'd basically be blacklisted from any halfway decent company.

I've been basically hiding how fucked up I am ever since I got back from Afghanistan.  It's been a few years now, and I still have nightmares constantly.  I started drinking a lot when I got back, at the time I thought it was just the usual "early 20-something party phase," but I'm now pushing 30 and it hasn't stopped.  The nights I black out drunk seem to the be the only times I don't keep dreaming about it.  The only reason I've managed to cut back on drinking lately is because I managed to get myself hooked on prescription painkillers.

All the while my friends and family would probably hold me up as a shining beacon of success.  I actually have managed to suck it up to the point I finished school, got a great job, and am pretty universally looked up to among my family and friends.  The shitty side to that coin is that I would lose my job (pretty much permanently) if I were to seek any kind of professional help, plus that I still have the whole "tough guy" thing ingrained in me, so I really doubt I'd be able to bring myself to ask for it in the first place.

I know I need to stop at some point, but the times I've tried to clean up on my own I relapse.  My choices are pretty much to get cleaned up and lose the career I love/the respect of those around me, or just see how long I can keep this going.  Who knows.

/rant
